title: Volleyball
statementMd:
Petya loves volleyball very much. One day he was running late for a volleyball match. Petya hasn't bought his own car yet, that's why he had to take a taxi. The city has $*n*$ junctions, some of which are connected by two-way roads. The length of each road is defined by some positive integer number of meters; the roads can have different lengths.

Initially each junction has exactly one taxi standing there. The taxi driver from the $*i*$-th junction agrees to drive Petya (perhaps through several intermediate junctions) to some other junction if the travel distance is not more than $*t*_{*i*}$ meters. Also, the cost of the ride doesn't depend on the distance and is equal to $*c*_{*i*}$ bourles. Taxis can't stop in the middle of a road. **Each taxi can be used no more than once. Petya can catch taxi only in the junction, where it stands initially.**

At the moment Petya is located on the junction $*x*$ and the volleyball stadium is on the junction $*y*$. Determine the minimum amount of money Petya will need to drive to the stadium.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 1000, 0 ≤ *m* ≤ 1000)$. They are the number of junctions and roads in the city correspondingly. The junctions are numbered from $1$ to $*n*$, inclusive. The next line contains two integers $*x*$ and $*y*$ ($1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ *n*$). They are the numbers of the initial and final junctions correspondingly. Next $*m*$ lines contain the roads' description. Each road is described by a group of three integers $*u*_{*i*}$, $*v*_{*i*}$, $*w*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*, 1 ≤ *w*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — they are the numbers of the junctions connected by the road and the length of the road, correspondingly. The next $*n*$ lines contain $*n*$ pairs of integers $*t*_{*i*}$ and $*c*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *t*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$), which describe the taxi driver that waits at the $*i*$-th junction — the maximum distance he can drive and the drive's cost. The road can't connect the junction with itself, but between a pair of junctions there can be more than one road. All consecutive numbers in each line are separated by exactly one space character.

## Output

If taxis can't drive Petya to the destination point, print "-1" (without the quotes). Otherwise, print the drive's minimum cost.

Please do not use the %lld specificator to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use cin, cout streams or the %I64d specificator.

## Note

An optimal way — ride from the junction 1 to 2 (via junction 4), then from 2 to 3. It costs 7+2=9 bourles.
statementZhMd:
Petya 非常喜欢排球。一天，他赶着去参加一场排球比赛。Petya 还没有买自己的汽车，因此他只好乘坐出租车。城市中有 $*n*$ 个路口，其中一些路口之间由双向道路连接。每条道路的长度由一个正整数（单位：米）给出，不同道路的长度可能不同。

最初，每个路口恰好停着一辆出租车。第 $*i*$ 个路口的出租车司机同意将 Petya 送到某个其他路口（途中可以经过若干个中间路口），前提是行驶距离不超过 $*t*_{*i*}$ 米。此外，乘车费用与距离无关，均为 $*c*_{*i*}$ 卢布。出租车不能在道路中途停车。**每辆出租车最多只能使用一次。Petya 只能在出租车最初停留的路口乘坐该出租车。**

现在，Petya 位于路口 $*x*$，排球场位于路口 $*y*$。请确定 Petya 到达排球场所需支付的最少费用。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 1000$，$0 ≤ *m* ≤ 1000$），分别表示城市中的路口数和道路数。路口编号为 $1$ 至 $*n*$（包括 $1$ 和 $*n*$）。

下一行包含两个整数 $*x*$ 和 $*y*$（$1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ *n*$），分别表示起始路口和终点路口的编号。接下来的 $*m*$ 行描述道路。每条道路由三个整数 $*u*_{*i}$、$*v*_{*i}$、$*w*_{*i}$（$1 ≤ *u*_{*i}, *v*_{*i} ≤ *n*$，$1 ≤ *w*_{*i} ≤ 10^{9}$）描述，分别表示由该道路连接的两个路口以及道路长度。接下来的 $*n*$ 行包含 $*n*$ 对整数 $*t*_{*i}$ 和 $*c*_{*i}$（$1 ≤ *t*_{*i}, *c*_{*i} ≤ 10^{9}$），描述在第 $*i*$ 个路口等待的出租车司机：他能够行驶的最大距离以及乘车费用。

道路不能连接一个路口自身，但一对路口之间可以有多条道路。每行中相邻的数字之间恰好由一个空格分隔。

## 输出格式

如果出租车无法将 Petya 送到目的地，请输出 “-1”（不含引号）。否则，输出乘车的最小费用。

请不要在 C++ 中使用 `%lld` 格式说明符读写 64 位整数。建议使用 cin、cout 流，或使用 `%I64d` 格式说明符。

## 说明

一种最优方案是从路口 1 乘车到路口 2（途经路口 4），然后从路口 2 乘车到路口 3。费用为 7+2=9 卢布。
